paper_metadata.title: Tensile and Low-Cycle Fatigue Behavior of Dissimilar Friction Welds of Alloy 718/Alloy 720Li
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance

evidence.quote: Nickel-chromium precipitation hardenable superalloy 718 is a high-strength and corrosion-resistant alloy
Both alloys are manufactured using different melting practices. Alloy 718 and alloy 720Li are double-melted using vacuum induction melting followed by vacuum arc remelting (VIM + V AR)
Samples of alloy 720Li were taken from a forged ring-shaped product, while alloy 718 rods were obtained from the supplier.
Samples of alloy 720Li were taken from a forged ring-shaped product, while alloy 718 rods were obtained from the supplier.
For FRW experiments, 15 mm diameter of rods were cut out using wire cut electrical discharge machining (EDM) from heat-treated parent materials of alloy 720Li and alloy 718.
The dissimilar FRW of 718/720Li were DA with the alloy 718 aging conditions, as given in Table 2.

attributes.morphology: cleavage structure with microvoid and crack

evidence.quote: The FRW joints in as-welded condition are failed at HAZ of alloy 718 region, and the fractography consisting of cleavage structure with the micro-void and crack is observed in Fig. 13(c).

attributes.morphology: grains coarsen and deformed in elongation direction

evidence.quote: the material underwent softening due to the thermal effects during high-temperature tests, which changes the material deformation behavior (the grains coarsen and deformed in the elongation direction).

The dissimilar 718/720Li FRW joint in as-welded condition exhibited 1265 MPa of tensile strength, which is lesser than the tensile strength of both parent materials.
The dissimilar 718/720Li FRW joints in the post-weld DA condition showed an 8.6% improvement in tensile strength (≈1374 MPa) than the as-welded condition samples.

The drop in hardness in the HAZ/TMAZ region of alloy 718 is attributed to the dissolution of strengthening precipitates during FRW.
The improvement in microhardness may be due to the re-precipitation of strengthening precipitates as a result of post-weld DA.
Dissimilar 718/720Li FRW joints in the as-welded condition showed lower hardness value at the HAZ region on the alloy 718 side due to the dissolution of strengthening precipitates during FRW.
Dissimilar 718/720Li FRW joint required post-weld DA for re-precipitation of strengthening precipitates for improved mechanical properties.
